newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's largest department store earnings rise.
newsitem.headline: Canada's largest department store earnings rise.

text.p: Hudson's Bay Co., Canada's largest department store chain, Thursday said earnings more than tripled in the third quarter and voiced optimism about the current quarter, which includes the holiday selling season.

Hudson's Bay, owner of Bay department stores and the Zellers discount chain, earned C$8.1 million ($6 million) or C$0.14 a share in the quarter ended Oct. 31, from C$2.2 million ($1.6 million) or Canadian 4 cents a share in the 1995 period.
Sales edged up to C$1.47 billion ($1.10 billion) from C$1.46 billion ($1.09 billion).

"We are optimistic about continued improvement in the crucial fourth quarter," the Toronto-based company said. "The retail climate should benefit from the combination of low rates of interest and inflation and from tax reductions for many consumers."

Canada's central bank has cut short-term interest rates by 5 points since May 1995. Canadian inflation is about 1.2 percent and the government of Ontario, Canada's most populous province, recently cut taxes.
For the first nine months of the year, Hudson's Bay lost C$44.9 million ($33.5 million) or C$0.76 a share compared to a year-earlier loss of C$6.5 million ($4.9 million) or C$0.11 a share.
The company took a C$64 million ($47.8 million) restructuring charge in the first quarter.
